title: Study Plan
statement: A student must study n topics, 0 to n − 1. Each pair [a, b] in rules means topic a must come before topic b. Return the study order that takes every topic; when several topics are available, always take the smallest number first. Return an empty list if no order exists.

keyPoints: Keep available topics (in-degree 0) in a min-heap
Always take the smallest, lower its neighbours' in-degrees, add newly free ones
Fewer than n taken means a cycle: return []
edgeCases: Topics with no rules mixed with chains
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Each round, scan all topics for the smallest free one: O(V² + E)

hints: Kahn's algorithm picks any topic with no remaining requirements. How do you make it pick the smallest?
Keep the free topics in a min-heap instead of a plain queue.
Pop the smallest, lower its neighbours' in-degrees, and push those that reach 0.
